brand_focus: Cooking tips, recipes, and marinades with AI-styled ingredient photography. Audience is Europe-first, US a strong second. Goal: grow followers fast-but-safe by making every post highly shareable (sent to a friend) and saveable.

slots.note: w1-18 is the highest-volume confirmed slot (7 posts, avg reach 1.7) — strongest statistical anchor in the dataset. Keeping quick-dinner here as the account's most reliable reach theme.
w2-12 produced reach 2.0 on 1 post — highest single-slot reach observed. Marinade is brand-core and has the largest post count (8); continuing to build sample at this lunchtime slot.
w3-12 avg reach 1.7 on 3 posts — confirmed mid-week lunchtime performer tied for second-best reach. Technique carousels are natural save-bait; deepening sample here.

w5-10 produced reach 2.0 on 1 post; proxying to Thursday morning as the adjacent high-browse window. Quick-dinner earns a second slot as the account's highest-reach theme. Sauce (avg reach 1.5, 6 posts, zero engagement across all signals) remains retired.

content_plan.quick-dinner: A complete weeknight dinner built around one hero ingredient that comes together fast. Slide 1: hero shot of the finished dish — rich colour, glossy sauce, clean negative space, pure food photography with absolutely no text, numbers, or labels anywhere on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay of raw ingredients loosely arranged by colour and texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: two-beat visual sequence showing one key technique moment (e.g. a vigorous sear, sauce reducing in pan) followed by the plated result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: tight close-up of texture and colour that makes the dish feel craveable and achievable. ALL ingredient quantities, timing, steps, swaps, and any written information belong in the caption only.
content_plan.marinade: One complete marinade built around a single protein or seasonal occasion. Slide 1: hero shot of the marinated, deeply coloured, glistening protein on a clean dark or neutral surface — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, or labels anywhere. Slide 2: aesthetic flat-lay of raw marinade ingredients grouped loosely by colour and texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: visual process contrast — protein submerging into the marinade liquid, then the vivid colour and sheen transformation after marinating — no overlaid text or graphics. Final slide: finished plated dish in warm directional light, garnished but not cluttered. ALL ratios, quantities, timing, substitution tips, and step information belong in the caption exclusively.
content_plan.technique: One foundational cooking technique relevant to home cooks — e.g. how to build a fond, reverse-sear, bloom spices, or emulsify a pan sauce. Slide 1: hero shot of the dramatic visual payoff of the technique (e.g. a perfectly seared crust, a glossy emulsified sauce) — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, labels, or graphics anywhere. Slide 2: flat-lay or close-up of the key tools or ingredients that make the technique work — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: two-beat before/after visual sequence showing the technique mid-action and the finished result — no text overlays. Final slide: close-up detail of texture, colour, or finish that makes the result unmistakably worth learning the technique. ALL explanations, ratios, timing, troubleshooting tips, and step-by-step instructions belong in the caption exclusively.

caption_strategy: Every caption must earn a save and a send before it earns a like. Open with a single punchy hook line that names the dish and its main appeal (e.g. 'The marinade that made me stop buying store-bought sauce'). Follow immediately with the full, usable recipe or technique in the caption body — exact quantities, timings, swaps, and troubleshooting — because all text-based information lives here, never on the image. Close with a low-friction CTA that prompts sharing: 'Send this to the person who needs it this week' or 'Save it before Friday dinner panic hits.' Write in plain, conversational English; use line breaks generously for scannability. Weave in search-friendly keywords naturally (e.g. 'quick chicken marinade,' 'weeknight pasta,' 'pan sauce technique') so the post surfaces in Instagram keyword search.
hashtag_strategy: Use exactly 3–5 hashtags per post, placed at the end of the caption after the CTA. Prioritise mid-size, specific tags (100k–2M posts) over massive generic ones — e.g. #weeknightdinner, #marinaderecipe, #cookingtechnique, #homecooking, #easydinner. Avoid oversaturated tags like #food or #recipe (500M+ posts) where new accounts are invisible. Rotate the set slightly each post to test discoverability, but always anchor on one theme-specific tag. Hashtags are a minor lever; invest most caption-writing effort in keyword-rich natural language rather than hashtag volume.
learnings: After 22 posts and 115 days, all sends, saves, and follows remain at zero across every theme and slot — reach is real but nothing is converting. The priority signal to chase is any non-zero send or save, not raw reach. Do not raise cadence; hold at 4/week until at least one theme or slot records a save or send. The two slots with reach 2.0 (w2-12, w5-10) are worth protecting. Sauce is retired (6 posts, bottom reach, no engagement). Caption quality is now the single highest-leverage variable: every caption must deliver a complete, usable recipe and an explicit share or save CTA.
